hook.text: Google bought YouTube in 2006 for $1.65 billion. Critics said it was absurdly overpriced.

buildup.text: YouTube was 18 months old with 100 million daily video views, zero profit, and massive copyright lawsuit risk.

discovery.text: Google saw what others missed: video would dominate the internet. Owning the platform meant owning the future of media.

twist.text: YouTube lost money for years. Google subsidized it with search profits until advertising finally made it profitable.

climax.text: The best acquisitions look expensive on day one and cheap by year ten.

punchline.text: $1.65 billion in 2006, $31 billion yearly now. The best deal ever.

quiz.question: Why was Google's purchase of YouTube initially criticized?
options: The $1.65 billion price seemed too high for a young, unprofitable platform

details.summary: Google acquired YouTube for 1.65 billion dollars in 2006 when the video platform was barely a year old and had no clear path to profitability. It became one of the most successful acquisitions in tech history, now generating over 30 billion annually.
details.whyItMatters: The YouTube acquisition shows how investment banking advisory applies to tech deals where traditional valuation metrics fail. The price seemed absurd in 2006 but proved to be perhaps the greatest bargain in tech M&A history.
takeaways: Google paid 1.65 billion dollars for a company with no revenue model
YouTube now generates over 30 billion dollars in annual advertising revenue
The deal was structured as an all-stock transaction

faq.question: Why did Google pay so much for a company with no revenue?
faq.answer: Google recognized YouTube's explosive user growth and its potential as an advertising platform. The acquisition eliminated a competitor to Google Video and gave Google control over the dominant online video platform.

faq.question: How did YouTube become so profitable?
faq.answer: Google integrated its advertising technology with YouTube's massive audience. Pre-roll ads, display ads, and eventually a subscription service transformed a money-losing platform into one of the most profitable properties on the internet.
